Hi Sasha — thanks for the clear list. High level answers below; I'm attaching a redline of the Order Form and our wipe verification procedure for Legal to review.

1) Grace windows: Redwood's standard backup retention after account termination is 90 days. We support bespoke windows down to 30 days for customers that need shorter retention; that is a negotiable Order Form term (we'll mark it as "Backup purge window" in the redline). For pilot customers we can set the backup purge to 30 days with a billing note.

2) Scope of deletion: our deletion process covers: primary persistent stores (customer data blobs, metadata indexes), ephemeral KV caches (cleared on deprovision), and model request logs tied to customer tokens. System-level backups and snapshots are included in the backup purge window — they are scheduled and expunged according to the Order Form term. Note: derived model artifacts (models trained by customers on private infra) are not applicable in hosted plans; if Meridian requires explicit handling of derivative artifacts we can add language.

3) Wipe verification: we provide a deletion attestation that includes: deletion job ID, timestamps for job start and completion, list of affected object keys, and a signed statement from the Redwood custodian. For higher assurance we can include a hash-certification for the object list and correlate with audit log entries. We can deliver the attestation as a PDF certificate and expose an API endpoint for programmatic verification (read-only) for one year post-deletion.

Next steps: I've attached "Meridian_OrderForm_v2_redline.pdf" with a proposed Order Form clause for a 30-day bespoke backup purge and draft language for the attestation. I've also attached "Wipe_Verification_Procedure.docx" with the admin-level operational steps. Can you confirm Procurement/Legal's preferred wording and whether the 30-day bespoke window is acceptable? If so, I'll route the redline to Redwood Legal and send a DocuSign link.

Hi Sasha — quick technical rundown to support the attestation text Rachel sent.

- Deletion workflow: when an account decomm request is issued we enqueue a coordinated deletion job. Primary object stores are deleted within 48 hours under normal conditions (this removes pointers, metadata, and issues object-level delete ops).

- Backups & snapshots: backups are immutable snapshots stored in a cold tier. The backup purge window controls when we garbage-collect shadow copies. For the bespoke 30-day option we run a background sweep at day 30+0–24h to remove snapshot manifests and then trigger object reclamation to clear the cold-store indexes; full physical reclamation of underlying blocks follows provider garbage-collection schedule (we include that note in the Order Form).

- Ephemeral caches / KV: KV caches are cleared on deprovision; there's no replica in backup storage for transient caches.

- Audit logs & attestation data: audit logs relevant to the deletion job (job ID, operator id, timestamps, object keys) are stored in our immutably-signed logging service for 365 days by default; we can extend retention by request in the Order Form. The attestation package will reference the job ID and a cryptographic signature that Legal can validate against our public key.

- SLA on deletion completion: we can commit to primary deletion within 48 hours and start backup purge within the agreed window (e.g., 30 days). We will include a clause that the customer will receive a signed attestation within 5 business days of job completion.

Attached: "Deletion_Procedure_Summary.pdf" — includes pseudocode for job lifecycle, sample audit log entries, and mapping of Order Form language to system events.

Happy to hop on a 20-min call to walk Legal & Security through the attestation format.
